Replay

Carom and beam queries

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Carom2 for the defined bouncing-shell motion rule and beam helpers for closed-segment hit queries. Carom2 is a value-owned position/velocity pair. carom2_step advances it against static AABBs and arena bounds, with caller-provided time, restitution and face clearance. It implements the original Scrapyard shell law: up to three cover legs, axis-normal reflection, then arena-wall clamp/reflection. The caller owns fuse, contact detection, damage and presentation.

Odin
body := p.Carom2{shot.position, shot.velocity}
if !p.carom2_step(&body, 1, 0.72, 0.1, arena_bounds, cover_boxes[:]) {
    r.abort(ctx)
    return
}
shot.position, shot.velocity = body.position, body.velocity

Positions use pixels and velocities use pixels per tick; time/clearance use ticks. Invalid finite/bounds/coefficient inputs reject without changing the body. An origin inside cover can exit. first_face2 queries the nearest strict entry before the time limit and returns the face normal. Its inputs must already be valid.

beam_circle implements the original lance/mender judge: closest point on a closed segment versus a target circle. Its fraction orders targets by center projection. Use segment_circle instead when the desired rule is first surface contact.

tests/replay_carom/run.sh compares 72 motion traces (300 steps each; four layouts, six launch cases, three frame durations) and 513 beam judgments against the original expressions compiled in isolation. The extracted motion block excludes node/trail presentation and fuse/contact damage; those are tested in the game. Cached original results permit standalone repository tests; REPLAY_REQUIRE_BASELINE=1 requires the sibling source too. Native boundaries and freestanding WASM checking pass.

These helpers define a reproducible kinematic rule for the authoritative/co-op runner. They do not establish cross-platform deterministic P2P for floating-point worlds or reproduce every aspect of the original render-frame grenade simulation.
